Keysight Technologies reported revenue of $1.85 billion, net income of $397 million, a gross margin of 65.87 percent and a net margin of 21.51 percent for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, which the results release describes as a record quarter with an improved full-year outlook [D1]. Within that total, the Communications Solutions Group produced $1.35 billion of revenue and $458 million of operating income, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group produced $501 million of revenue and $155 million of operating income, giving total segment operating income of $613 million [D1]. The balance sheet carries total assets of $11.92 billion and shareholders equity of $6.57 billion against net debt of $141 million [D1].

The bull case rests on the gap between a forward price to earnings of 20.66 and a trailing price to earnings of 45.89 on trailing earnings per share of 7.38 [D7]. Technically, the shares are in an uptrend, closing at 333.42 above a 20-day average of 330.47, a 50-day average of 326.21 and a 200-day average of 289.31, with a 14-day relative strength index of 54.21 [D2]. Analyst price targets are often overly optimistic and rarely indicate where a share price is heading, so the bullish targets on the stock should be treated with skepticism [D7].

The bear case accepts the same results and disputes their durability, pointing to management's own statement that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue, that the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago, and that revenue conversion will be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D3]. Management also cautioned that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat, which raises the comparison bar for profitability in the next report [D3]. On the chart, the close of 333.42 sits barely above the high edge of immediate support at 332.78, while immediate resistance at 366.41 is rated at a strength of three against a support strength of 59 [D2].

The plan is therefore to hold the constructive view while the uptrend, the 20-day average of 330.47 and the support shelf down to 300.87 remain intact, and to treat resistance at 366.41 as the level that would confirm the trend [D2]. On fundamentals, the plan waits for evidence that supply has stopped governing the conversion of demand into revenue before adding exposure, and for the Communications Solutions Group to build on its $1.35 billion quarter [D3][D1]. The plan would step aside if gross margin falls below 65.87 percent or net margin below 21.51 percent once the one-time tariff benefit is gone [D1]. Further out, the plan keeps the 6G opportunity in view, since it is expected to be larger than the 5G cycle and depends on customers moving from exploratory research into funded development programs [D4].
